title: Pictures first, video last
rule: Approve the start and end pictures of a clip before spending any video generation on it.
why: Image generation is cheap and fixing blocking after video exists means regenerating the video.
how: Storyboard each scene as stills, choose one, then send only approved stills to the video model.

monofilm.where: Scenes: Stage then Pictures then Pack; Pack is locked until pictures are approved

title: Lock references before any shot
rule: Make and approve character, place and prop references once, before the first clip is generated.
why: Consistency re-rolls are the biggest credit drain; one creator estimates an hour of reference work saves about five hours of generation.
how: Train or choose the identity first; reuse the same set in every prompt; do not start partway through.

monofilm.where: People and Places steps; anchor face and place plates feed every picture

title: Chain clips on matching frames
rule: Make the last frame of one clip the first frame of the next, and never break the chain.
why: Breaking the start-frame chain makes the character and place drift; identity degrades fast over long single generations.
how: Keep clips short; use the approved end picture as the next clip start picture.

monofilm.where: End pictures are drawn from the picture before; last state of a scene is first of the next (README, What keeps a film from drifting)

title: Short clips with one purpose
rule: Keep each clip to one action and a length the model holds well (about 4-8 s); replace a weak clip instead of redoing a sequence.
why: Short clips force clarity, and the last frame is respected less in long ones.
how: Plan six to eight clips per piece; for tight endpoints use 4 second clips.

monofilm.where: Scene made of clips up to 8 s (MAX_CLIP in public/js/pack.js)

title: Budget for overgeneration
rule: Plan to generate several times the finished runtime and show that cost before the first paid call.
why: Reported ratios are about 3 generations per usable shot, 3-5x footage, and up to 300:1 for a hard Sora short; hidden retakes are the real cost.
how: Show attempts times unit cost, not the price of one generation.

monofilm.where: Credit budget and plan price shown before a fix (README, Under the hood)
monofilm.idea: Show expected attempts per clip using shot-risk class (wf-p-006) in the price preview.

title: Budget retakes by shot type
rule: Give multi-character contact, dialogue, POV and continuity-heavy clips more attempts and more budget than simple single-subject clips.
why: Contact shots break far faster than static single-character ones.
how: Flag these clips in the Brief and raise the retry allowance and credit estimate.

monofilm.where: MAX_ATTEMPTS is a flat 3 in public/js/pack.js
monofilm.idea: Classify each clip by risk (people touching, dialogue, POV) and scale the attempt budget and shown price.

title: Judge takes as a set
rule: Generate a small batch of variants per clip and choose the best, rather than tweaking one prompt after each single output.
why: Run-to-run variance can exceed prompt-to-prompt variance, so single samples mislead.
how: Four variations per prompt, judged side by side; lock the winner before moving on.

monofilm.where: Three candidates for start and end pictures; clips get next seed up to three tries (get_clip, retryAdvice)
monofilm.idea: Offer a batch of takes per clip on Pack, compared side by side.

title: Expect a large discard share
rule: Plan on discarding most generated clips (reported 70-80 percent) and treat it as a budget line, not a failure.
why: Documented productions kept about a quarter of what they generated.
how: Budget by total generated seconds and salvage the best seconds of several takes.

monofilm.where: Up to three attempts per clip with advice (retryAdvice in public/js/pack.js)

title: Draft cheap, finish expensive
rule: Explore on a cheap or fast model tier and render only approved shots on the premium tier.
why: Tiers differ by 4-8x in price per second; four cheap drafts plus one fast final beat iterating on the mid tier.
how: Mute audio on drafts if sound is added later; confirm the cost before running.

monofilm.where: list_generators describes weaknesses only
monofilm.idea: Add a draft/final tier note and price per second to each generator profile.

title: Run the hardest shot first
rule: Generate the riskiest clip of a scene first as a proof; if it holds, the rest usually will.
why: It tells you early whether the plan is feasible before credits go to easy shots.
how: Pick the clip with most characters, contact or camera motion; only then do the others.

monofilm.where: Clips are made in order
monofilm.idea: Order the Pack queue so the riskiest clip is tested first.

title: Change one thing per retry
rule: When a take fails, change one variable (or add one correction) and keep the rest the same.
why: Changing many things hides what worked; a fix prompt that keeps everything else avoids new defects.
how: State the keep-the-same part first, then the single change.

monofilm.where: review_take returns what to add to the prompt; get_clip gives next seed and advice (retryAdvice)

title: Change approach after repeated failure
rule: If a shot keeps failing, change the method (different model, split the shot, voice-over cut) instead of repeating the prompt.
why: Repeating the same attempt wastes credits; one creator solved a failing dialogue scene by switching model and editing.
how: After two fails recommend splitting the clip or another generator.

monofilm.where: Advice grows over the three tries; flat limit of three attempts
monofilm.idea: On the third failure, suggest splitting the clip or switching generator.

title: Pick the tool per shot type
rule: Use different generators for different shot types rather than one for everything.
why: Models differ: dialogue, faces, environments and camera control each favour a different tool.
how: Record each generator strengths in its profile and choose per clip.

monofilm.where: list_generators and the generator option on get_clip
monofilm.idea: Suggest a generator per clip from its type (dialogue, wide, close-up).

title: Words never fight the picture
rule: Do not use text to override a strong reference; fix the reference instead.
why: A reference with three monitors kept three monitors whatever the prompt said.
how: Edit the picture and re-approve it, then re-prompt.

monofilm.where: A clip words never describe a character again once it has a start picture (README)

title: Human checkpoints before each spend
rule: Make a person approve script, shot list, character sheets and look frames before generating, and the final cut at the end.
why: Errors in early assets repeat in every shot built on them.
how: Lock the next step until the previous is approved; keep approvals under the human name.

monofilm.where: Only a person can approve; Roll camera approvals are recorded by name; each page locks the next button

title: Run a full continuity playthrough
rule: Before delivery watch the whole cut for identity drift, spatial errors, flicker and audio sync, and mark composite shots.
why: Skipping the final review is called the most common mistake.
how: Compare first, middle and last stills of each scene.

monofilm.where: Continuity review of the plan; review_take per clip; npm run measure finds cuts, jumps, frozen tail
monofilm.idea: Add a whole-film playthrough check on the Ship page.

title: Check the clip end and trim a frozen tail
rule: Measure each returned clip for cuts, jumps and a frozen end, and trim the dead frames.
why: Only a part of each generation is used (about 5 of 15 s) and endpoints drift, mostly at the last frame.
how: Trim to where the motion stops plus a short settle.

monofilm.where: scripts/measure-take.mjs (hold, keep, smooth, cuts); tailHold in public/js/pack.js

title: Same aspect ratio for both end pictures
rule: Give first and last frame pictures the same aspect ratio as the requested clip.
why: Mismatched ratios give awkward crops and rough interpolation.
how: Make both at the clip shape; crop before upload.

monofilm.where: Pack trims pictures to what the generator accepts (targets in sceneEntries)
monofilm.idea: Warn when start and end pictures differ in shape.

title: Upscale first, then one grade
rule: Upscale selected clips before grading, and apply one identical texture and grade pass across all of them.
why: Each generation has its own white balance, and different models look sharp or plasticky in different ways; a grade on pre-upscale footage can shift.
how: Match every clip to a hero clip on scopes, then add blur, grain and last a LUT.

monofilm.where: Pack ships files and subtitles only
monofilm.idea: Add a finishing note to the Ship pack: upscale, hero match, shared grain.

title: Upscale only the shots that make the cut
rule: Generate at low resolution for exploration and upscale only the chosen shots.
why: Air Head was made at 480p then upscaled; but details you liked at low resolution can change when re-rendered high.
how: Do not re-render at high resolution; upscale the approved low-res clip.

monofilm.idea: Add a generate-low-then-upscale option to generator profiles.

title: Generate audio per scene
rule: Make dialogue, ambience and score per scene, not for the whole film in one pass, and avoid adding audio after a clip to keep sync.
why: Audio added after rendering breaks lip alignment; per-scene sound keeps genre register.
how: If lip sync drifts regenerate the sequence.

monofilm.where: Sound page works one clip at a time with lines and sounds

title: Fix known generator quirks in post and record them
rule: Write each generator observed habits (unrequested slow motion, extra strings or faces, colour changes) in its profile and retime or clean in post.
why: Air Head needed retiming, face removal and recolouring on nearly every shot.
how: Add a negative line to the prompt and a post step.

monofilm.where: list_generators adapts words to a model known weaknesses
monofilm.idea: Add a retime/clean checklist to profiles.

title: Keep a human hand in the work
rule: Keep some human-made material (design, voice, music) and record how much AI was used.
why: Purely AI work often cannot be copyrighted; the hybrid films keep humans central.
how: Mark which parts are human in the manifest.

monofilm.idea: Record a human-versus-generated note per asset in the manifest.

title: Use first-last frames and references where the tool allows
rule: Use first/last-frame and reference inputs of the open tools (Wan, LTX) for the same control the hosted tools give, and know the limits.
why: The first frame is held closely, the last less so; Wan wants a high VRAM class for 14B models.
how: Pick Wan TI2V-5B (24 GB) for local drafts, LTX distilled for fast iteration.

monofilm.where: Pack carries start and end pictures and reference files per clip
monofilm.idea: Add open-source ComfyUI entries to list_generators.
